epic.title: External Website Channels and CMS Interoperability
epic.description: Make DPF the canonical governed business/content operating layer while projecting approved content and structured business facts to externally hosted website/CMS channels. WordPress is the first provider; the architecture remains provider-neutral and does not bundle hosting, public URL, CDN, theme, or plugin-runtime operations.
epic.scopeRationale: Cross-archetype platform connector, publication, authority, security, and UX substrate; individual organizations opt in to provider connections.

items.title: Publish WordPress interoperability architecture, claims, runbook, and adoption evidence
items.body: Parent BI-F50B1E46. Complete the operator/admin guide, connection/revocation/recovery runbook, supported-capability matrix, product-positioning claims, EA/SysML interfaces/allocations/verification cases, and adoption/quality measurement. Allowed claim: DPF operates behind an existing WordPress site and can publish governed content. Prohibit full CMS/hosting/plugin/two-way-sync claims. Acceptance: docs are linked/indexed; architecture parity is green; runbook covers 401/403/404/429/5xx, drift, queued actions, and disconnect; telemetry reports connection/publication/drift/recovery without content/secret labels; first reference-install exercise has receipts. Depends on executable slices for final evidence, but documentation skeleton and claim guardrails may ship earlier. Reserve ~20% for consolidating duplicate connector/publication documentation.

items.title: Deliver the WordPress connection, health, preview, and drift UX
items.body: Parent BI-F50B1E46. Add WordPress to the existing /platform/tools/integrations family and one provider detail route; add contextual Publish to website actions only in eligible Marketing/Storefront surfaces. First viewport shows site, status, supported actions, authority sentence, and exactly one next action. Connection form asks URL/username/Application Password, checks before save, then previews capabilities and draft-vs-live policy. Acceptance: shared form/report-kit/token primitives; no new global nav/dashboard/KPIs; credentials never redisplayed; fresh/permission/REST/credential/drift/disconnected states each have one honest recovery; preview+confirmation for writes; desktop/narrow browser task, accessibility, route budgets, style/theme scans, and measured ux-fit manifest. Depends on connector and first publication path. Reserve ~20% to extract/converge repeated integration connection-state UI.

items.title: Deliver governed WordPress channel projection without making DPF a public CMS host
items.body:
## Problem
Many adopting organizations already run WordPress. DPF currently has no governed way to discover that site, assess which WordPress capabilities are absorbed versus retained, import inventory/read-only context, or project approved DPF content and structured business facts into it.

## Outcome
Deliver WordPress as the first external website channel on DPF's unified connector and outbound-publication substrate. DPF remains canonical for business facts, content intent, approval, audit, and scheduling. WordPress remains canonical for public presentation: themes, blocks/layout, permalink/SEO settings, hosting, CDN, and plugin-rendered behavior.

## Architectural guardrails
- No bundled WordPress/PHP/database runtime, public DPF URL, CDN, theme engine, or general-purpose CMS data model.
- Start one-way: DPF -> WordPress for approved publication; authenticated polling for discovery/drift. Webhooks and a thin WordPress plugin are optional later increments.
- Reuse IntegrationCredential custody, connector definitions/checkpoints/audit, OutboundDraft/Approval/ScheduledOutboundAction/OutboundPublication, media storage, and owning domain records.
- Resolve incumbent posture by normalized provider identity plus integration category/capability; never arbitrary provider-name-only findFirst.
- Per-resource authority and conflict behavior are explicit. No silent two-way merge and no WordPress content overwriting DPF operational truth.
- User-supplied site URLs require SSRF/DNS-rebinding defenses, HTTPS, bounded redirects, content sanitization, least privilege, safe errors, and auditable external writes.
- Reserve approximately 20% of every implementation slice for convergence/refactoring and invariant coverage.

## Initial scope
1. Provider/category identity and absorption-posture correctness.
2. WordPress REST discovery, health, auth, bounded incremental read.
3. Approved posts/pages/media publication with idempotent external identity mapping.
4. Structured storefront/catalog projection with preview, drift, and authority rules.
5. Setup/health/publication UX in the existing Integrations route family plus contextual Marketing/Storefront actions.
6. EA/parity evidence, positioning claims, operational docs, and adoption measurement.

## Acceptance
A founder/operator can connect a supported HTTPS WordPress site with a dedicated application password, see a truthful capability/authority preview, publish an approved DPF item as a WordPress draft or scheduled/public post, see its external URL and audit receipt, detect later external modification without silent overwrite, and disconnect/revoke credentials. Fresh install/unavailable/permission/plugin-conflict states provide one honest recovery action. Tests prove idempotency, approval enforcement, pagination/cursors, SSRF controls, sanitization, authority, and no duplicate publication.
